title: Atomic token and component curation protocol for lifecycle and deprecation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a pragmatic, enforceable protocol for managing design tokens and UI components across the Redwood design system. The protocol will cover contribution flows, RFC expectations, automated checks, versioning semantics for tokens, chart/table/button lifecycle (onboarding, backward-compatible changes, deprecation, and retirement), migration guidance for engineers, and visualization of impact in the Console. Goal: reduce surprise regressions, make deprecations low-friction for integrators, and provide a single source of truth for maintainers.
acceptance_criteria: A written protocol document describing: contribution steps, required RFC template fields, review checklist, deprecation windows, and migration helpers
A review checklist committed to the design repo as CODEOWNERS/PR template
A codemod plan (MD) and example script for token aliasing included in the repo with a sample run log
Automated CI checks added for token naming, accessibility assertions, and visual regression baseline for changed components
A short migration guide for engineering teams and a Console dashboard mock showing token/component deprecation status
review_checklist: Token naming follows semantic namespace (e.g., color.bg.surface, spacing.2) and matches token taxonomy doc
Alias path provided for any token rename with codemod instructions and automated tests
Design spec update: Figma file link, usage examples, and responsive states for component changes
Accessibility validation: contrast, keyboard focus, ARIA where applicable
Integration impact assessment: list of likely affected endpoints, SDK calls, and server-side rendering concerns
Performance estimate: size/paint/regression implications for charts and tables
Rollback and canary plan: feature flag gating or CSS variable fallback strategy
Telemetry hooks: events to track adoption and errors, plus a Console query example
Deprecation notice text and timeline included in PR description

2025-03-18 - Decision logged: Use semantic token versioning vMAJOR.MINOR (tokens will carry a namespace version); opt-in deprecation header in Console rather than automatic enforcement for first 6 months
decision_log: Adopt token aliasing strategy: when renaming, we add a new key and keep the old key as an alias for one deprecation cycle
Deprecation windows: 12 weeks for removals, 6 weeks for non-breaking renames; emergency removals require cross-org approval
RFC process: all token/component changes that touch more than one package require an RFC with migration plan and estimated ETA
Automated checks: stylelint for token keys, visual regression for component snapshots, accessibility audit on merge
Versioning: use semantic namespace for tokens; components will follow package semver in the monorepo
